Question
========
Data can be structured, semi-structured or unstructured, depending on how strictly it is organized. Which statement correctly describes how the degree of structure relates to the degree of flexibility?

Answerlist
----------
* The stricter the format of a dataset, the more flexible it becomes to work with.
* The stricter the format of a dataset, the less flexible it becomes, since every entry must fit a fixed layout.
* Structure and flexibility always increase together.
* How structured a dataset is has nothing to do with how flexible it is.


Solution
========
The degree of structure and the degree of flexibility work against each other. A strictly structured format, such as a relational database table, leaves very little room for exceptions, missing values or nested information, since every row has to follow the same predefined columns. Semi-structured and unstructured formats give up some of that strictness in exchange for more flexibility.

----------
* False
* True

* False
